items.body_md:
On August 10, the FTX Recovery Trust filed two omnibus objections to claims — one public (Dkt. 36106) and one sealed (Dkt. 36104), with a redacted public counterpart (Dkt. 36105) — setting a response deadline of September 10, 2026 and a hearing for September 17 at 9:30 a.m. before Judge Owens in Wilmington. The sealed filing is notable: the Trust's standard omnibus objection practice has proceeded almost entirely on the public docket, so a sealed objection with a simultaneously filed redacted version indicates the targeted claims involve confidential identifying information or settlement terms that the Trust has reason to protect from public disclosure. The grounds and claim count are not ascertainable from the public record. The public objection (Dkt. 36106) is a standard omnibus in the Trust's ongoing reconciliation campaign, which has now reached at least 186 omnibus objections across the life of the case — the September 17 hearing date aligns with the next omnibus hearing already on the calendar (August 19 is the upcoming omnibus hearing; the September date is a newly calendared session).

Also filed August 10, Kroll filed the quarterly claims register (Dkt. 36102), a routine administrative snapshot of the current state of the claims docket. Seven claim transfers appeared the same day: FTXCREDITOR, LLC transferred four separate redacted claims to Grand Teton C II, LLC (Dkts. 36093–36096) and one to itself (Dkt. 36092); Cherokee Acquisition transferred Claim No. 8231 to GreenWulf Master Fund, LP (Dkt. 36107); and Dingdingke Ltd. recorded one additional transfer (Dkt. 36090). The volume — five transfers to Grand Teton alone in a single day through FTXCREDITOR, LLC — suggests a coordinated portfolio acquisition by a secondary-market buyer consolidating positions ahead of what the Trust has signaled will be continued distributions. Individual transfer amounts are redacted and claim values are not ascertainable from the docket entries. Dkts. 36088, 36089, 36103, and 36109 are Kroll affidavits of mailing related to prior docket entries and carry no independent weight on recovery.

The sealed omnibus objection pair (Dkts. 36104/36105) is the item to watch before the September 10 objection deadline. Affected claimants who received notice but whose claims are sealed will need to respond without the benefit of a public record to compare against — a procedural asymmetry that could draw objections from claimants who argue inadequate disclosure. The next concrete milestone is the August 19 omnibus hearing before Judge Owens (Case No. 22-11068), which will address the queue of previously filed objections and any matters noticed for that session.

items.body_md:
On August 7, Next Claims Capital Limited filed a transfer of an unnamed claimant's allowed claim (Dkt. 36086), and separately, Cenjun Zhu filed a transfer of Claim No. 03428491 to Peng Xu (Dkt. 36085), both under Fed. R. Bankr. P. 3001(e)(2) in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware, Case No. 22-11068, before Judge Karen B. Owens. These are the only docket entries in the 72-hour window. No substantive filings, rulings, or orders moved across the docket this weekend.

Both transfers are routine secondary-market transactions. Their significance is structural rather than event-specific: institutional buyers and individual transferees continue acquiring allowed claims against a live distribution backdrop. 
Holders of allowed claims who do not successfully onboard with a distribution service provider within six months from the July 31, 2026 distribution date risk forfeiting their right to receive distributions on those claims
 — a deadline that creates near-term pressure on transferees to complete onboarding promptly. The Next Claims Capital transfer involves a redacted transferor, consistent with the docket's standard practice for claimants who have elected confidentiality. The Zhu-to-Xu transfer attaches a receipt (Dkt. 36085, Attachment 1), indicating the filing fee was paid and the transfer is procedurally complete. Neither transfer alters the aggregate recovery pool or the Trust's distribution mechanics.

The broader recovery posture remains shaped by the two developments reported last week: 
FTX's fifth creditor distribution of approximately $900 million commenced July 31, covering allowed Convenience and Non-Convenience claims under the Chapter 11 plan, with payments processed through BitGo, Kraken, and Payoneer for claimants who met the June 16 record date and completed pre-distribution requirements
. 
That payout lifts cumulative repayments since the wind-down began to nearly $10 billion.
 The Junho Bang settlement — 
in which the FTX Recovery Trust asked the Delaware bankruptcy judge to approve a deal with Bang's foreign representative that would return more than $160 million to the fraudster's victims
 — remains pending court approval; confirmation would appear as a signed order on the docket. 
The deal involves Soogeun Oh, the court-appointed receiver for Bang's estate; Bang was linked to funds deposited into high-volume FTX trading accounts sourced from a June 2022 crypto investment program; recovered funds are routed to victims through South Korean insolvency proceedings, and the agreement bars Bang and his affiliates from receiving any proceeds
 — __[Law360](https://www.law360.com/bankruptcy-authority/articles/2507863/ftx-deal-would-route-160m-to-victims-of-korean-fraudster)__, __[CoinCentral](https://coincentral.com/ftx-starts-900m-creditor-distribution-as-repayments-near-10b/)__. The next concrete milestone is the Bang settlement approval hearing; no date has been publicly confirmed, and it has not yet appeared on the docket as a scheduled matter.

items.lede: The 72-hour window produced light movement: two claim transfers, a fee examiner report, a Kroll mailing affidavit, and a cancellation of the August 7 hearing. None of these are substantive developments for recovery posture; the briefing is proportioned accordingly.
items.body_md:
The 72-hour window produced light movement: two claim transfers, a fee examiner report, a Kroll mailing affidavit, and a cancellation of the August 7 hearing. None of these are substantive developments for recovery posture; the briefing is proportioned accordingly.

The most consequential filing in the window is Dkt. 36084, Fee Examiner Katherine Stadler's report filed August 6, referencing related docket entries [29610], [29611], [29612], [29613], [29801], [29807], and [29847] — a cluster spanning Stadler's fee-review work from the early post-confirmation period through at least the first quarter of 2025. Stadler was appointed pursuant to D.I. 834 and has served as the court's independent check on professional compensation throughout the case. The August 6 report has not yet been described in secondary reporting, and its specific findings — fee amounts reviewed, reductions recommended, and any reserved objections — are unverified beyond the docket entry itself; confirmation of the substance will require the report document to appear on the Kroll claims portal or be described in subsequent court filings or coverage. For claimants, the practical significance of ongoing fee-examiner oversight is indirect but real: each dollar of professional compensation approved draws from the same distributable pool, and Stadler's reports have historically resulted in negotiated reductions across several retained professionals.

Dkt. 36082, filed August 6, cancelled the August 7 hearing outright rather than adjourning it. The amended notice of agenda for that hearing (Dkt. 36081, already covered) had listed matters for Judge Karen B. Owens in Courtroom 3, Wilmington. Cancellation, without a rescheduled date visible on the docket, is consistent with matters being resolved consensually or mooted before the hearing date — not an adverse development, but one that leaves the next scheduled court event unidentified from the docket as of this morning. Dkt. 36083, the Kroll mailing affidavit relating to Dkts. 36062 and 36063, is purely administrative — confirmation that required notice was served on the relevant parties. The two claim transfers in the window (Dkt. 36085, Cenjun Zhu, Claim No. 03428491, to Peng Xu; Dkt. 36086, a redacted transferor to Next Claims Capital Limited) continue the steady secondary-market activity that has characterized this case since plan confirmation. Both are standard Rule 3001(e)(2) assignments. The Next Claims Capital transfer involves a redacted transferor, consistent with the confidentiality elections that institutional claim purchasers routinely invoke; it does not signal anything unusual on its face.

On the distribution front, no new trust announcement has appeared in the window. The fifth distribution of approximately $900 million commenced July 31, bringing cumulative creditor repayments to approximately $10.9 billion; 
alongside the main creditor distribution, July 31 also saw a second payment from the Preferred Shareholder Remission Fund Trust to eligible preferred equity holders, totaling $18 million and bringing cumulative PSRFT payments to $95 million.
 
The FTX Recovery Trust has stated that additional record and payment dates will be announced in due course, with creditor representative Sunil Kavuri indicating that further distributions are anticipated in the October/December 2026 period and continuing through 2027 for creditors with pending or disputed claims.
 The next concrete milestone visible from the docket is confirmation of the substance of Stadler's August 6 report, which would ordinarily surface either through a fee hearing notice or a court order on the recommended allowances.
